veranderings.rede: A comma closing the long relative clause stops the reader running 'vertel' into its object.
'van ... geleer' can read as 'learned from the cities'; 'oor' makes clear they are what he learned about.

veranderings.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
veranderings.voor: wat mense gebruik het in plaas van munte van metaal
veranderings.na: wat mense in plaas van munte van metaal gebruik het
veranderings.rede: In a relative clause, standard Afrikaans puts the verb cluster at the end.

veranderings.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
veranderings.rede: AWS: no comma before 'en' joining two relative clauses inside one sentence.

veranderings.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
veranderings.na: wat mense gebruik het om water
veranderings.rede: Past tense, to match the first item's 'gebruik het' about the same people in the same book.

veranderings.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
veranderings.voor: as die stede wat hy in Europa
veranderings.na: as dié wat hy in Europa
veranderings.rede: Avoids repeating 'stede' twice in one short item.

veranderings.voor: Ná baie jare het hy die pad
veranderings.na: Ná baie jare het Marco Polo die pad
veranderings.rede: The block opens after a list, so the name makes clear who 'hy' is.

veranderings.voor: Sonder daardie boek sou ons byna niks van sy reise geweet het nie.
veranderings.na: Sonder daardie boek sou ons byna niks daarvan geweet het nie.
veranderings.rede: 'sy reise' appears in three sentences in a row; 'daarvan' removes the wooden repetition.

veranderings.voor: Die kopieë verskil van mekaar en party
veranderings.na: Die kopieë verskil van mekaar, en party
veranderings.rede: AWS: comma before 'en' joining two sentences, each with its own subject and verb.
'aanvaar ... as vasgestel' is stiff; 'as vasstaande feit' is the natural idiom with the same meaning.
'niemand ... enige' copies English 'no one ... any'; Afrikaans uses the indefinite article after a negative.

veranderings.voor: Marco Polo het in dieselfde tydperk as Mapungubwe in Asië gereis.
veranderings.na: In dieselfde tydperk as Mapungubwe het Marco Polo in Asië gereis.
veranderings.rede: As written, 'Mapungubwe in Asië' can read as one phrase, placing Mapungubwe in Asia; fronting the time phrase removes that misreading.

veranderings.voor: 'n Groep handelaars, diere en goedere wat saam op reis is.
veranderings.na: 'n Karavaan is 'n groep handelaars, diere en goedere wat saam op reis is.
veranderings.rede: Every other glossary entry in the lesson is a full sentence naming its term; this one is a fragment.

vlae.teks: Die boek vertel dat hy tyd by die hof van 'n magtige heerser deurgebring het.
vlae.rede: 'Die boek' is used here and in the list heading before any book is introduced; the book is only explained in 'Terug in Venesië'. The phrase is protected, so the writer would have to solve this, perhaps by mentioning the book earlier.

vlae.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
vlae.teks: Plekke waar sy gemaak word en waar speserye gekweek word.
vlae.rede: A Grade 6 reader will most likely read 'sy' as the pronoun 'she' and not as silk. A clearer word (for example 'systof') could shift the meaning from making silk to weaving it, which the protected entry treats as a fact-sensitive point, so the writer should choose the word.

vlae.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
vlae.teks: Papiergeld wat mense gebruik het ... / Ruiters wat briewe aangee ...
vlae.rede: The list switches between past tense (items 1 and 3) and present tense (items 2, 4 and 5). Only item 2 is proposed above; the writer may want one tense throughout.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: This wording is protected, but at that point in the lesson no book has been introduced, so 'Die boek' has nothing to refer to. 'Sy boek' or an earlier mention would fix it. See the flag.
